clippings.speaker: Howard Hawks
clippings.quote: I told John Wayne when we started to work together, ‘Duke, if you can make two good scenes and not annoy the audience for the rest of the film, you’ll be a star.’
clippings.title: An audience with Howard Hawks
clippings.context: Hawks interviewed by Joseph McBride and Michael Wilmington at the Chicago Film Festival in November 1970, printed in the Spring 1971 issue.

clippings.speaker: Howard Hawks
clippings.quote: So I said to Wayne, ‘Now, look, you go out there – if you forget your lines, just say anything, keep talking until I tell you to come on in. We’ll make the sound afterwards.’
clippings.title: An audience with Howard Hawks
clippings.context: Hawks describing the burial scene in Red River, where he had Wayne keep talking so the sound could be recorded afterwards while he waited for a cloud to pass.

clippings.speaker: Howard Hawks
clippings.quote: In Rio Bravo, Wayne hit a fellow across the face the most horrible way. Dean Martin said, ‘Hey, take it easy.’ And Wayne said, ‘I’m not gonna hurt him.’ The audience thought it was funny.
clippings.title: An audience with Howard Hawks
clippings.context: Hawks talking in November 1970 about the humour he found in Wayne's violence in Rio Bravo.

clippings.speaker: John Wayne
clippings.quote: 'You'll win an Academy Award,' [Hawks] said. 'Yeah, yeah,' I said. Instead, I played it as a strong man who was scared.
clippings.publication: Scott Eyman biography of John Wayne
clippings.title: John Wayne Wasn't A Fan Of The Image Howard Hawks Had In Mind For Him
clippings.context: Wayne recalling Hawks's pitch for Red River, where Hawks wanted him to play a 'big, blustering coward' and Wayne chose to play a strong man who was scared; quoted by SlashFilm from Scott Eyman's biography.

clippings.speaker: John Wayne
clippings.quote: If you say a funeral is funny, I’ll do a funeral.
clippings.title: An audience with Howard Hawks
clippings.context: Wayne's reply, as Hawks recounts it, after Hawks pitched him a comic finger-amputation scene for Red River that Wayne found unfunny.

notes: Hawks side is strong, all from one BFI interview (three separate passages). Wayne side is thin: no direct Wayne interview on Hawks was reachable (Playboy 1971 and Columbia oral history not accessible), so both Wayne quotes are secondhand; the SlashFilm one's original date is unverified. Academy speech db (047-24) has only Hawks's honorary-award speech, no usable Wayne text.
